4048.title: Mixed models: `merge_adapter()` merges nested adapters in reverse order, `unmerge_adapter()` then corrupts base weights
4048.body:
### System Info

PEFT main @ 7d6315ae, transformers 5.20.2, torch 2.14.1 (CPU for the repro; NVIDIA GB10 for the Qwen3-4B numbers), Python 3.12

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1

### Reproduction

When two adapters are stacked on the same layer in a `PeftMixedModel`, the forward pass applies the inner adapter first, e.g. `oft(lora(base))`. `merge_adapter()` iterates over `self.model.modules()` (`BaseTuner.merge_adapter`, `tuners_utils.py:1378`), which visits the outer layer first. For `oft(lora(base))`, the merged weight becomes `OFT(W) + ΔW_lora` instead of `OFT(W + ΔW_lora)`. `unmerge_adapter()` undoes OFT first and then subtracts `ΔW_lora`, which does not give back `W`.

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from peft import LoraConfig, OFTConfig, get_peft_model

torch.manual_seed(0)
base = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(8, 6)).eval()
W0 = base[0].weight.detach().clone()
x = torch.randn(4, 8)

model = get_peft_model(base, LoraConfig(target_modules=["0"], init_lora_weights=False), adapter_name="first", mixed=True)
model.add_adapter("second", OFTConfig(target_modules=["0"], init_weights=False, r=0, oft_block_size=2))
model.set_adapter(["first", "second"])
model.eval()

with torch.no_grad():
    y = model(x)
    model.merge_adapter()
    print("merged vs unmerged:", (model(x) - y).abs().max().item())       # 0.135, expected ~1e-7
    model.unmerge_adapter()
    print("after unmerge:", (model(x) - y).abs().max().item())            # 0.135, expected ~1e-7
    print("base weight restored:", torch.allclose(model.base_model.model[0].get_base_layer().weight, W0, atol=1e-6))  # False
```

`merge_and_unload()` gives the correct result for two adapters, because `MixedModel._unload_and_optionally_merge` merges the inner layer first. With three nested adapters it is also wrong whenever OFT is not the outermost adapter (4 of the 6 LoRA/OFT/LoHa orders): `merge_recursively` merges the middle layer, then the innermost, then the outermost, so the two inner layers are swapped.

The ordering only matters when a non-additive adapter like OFT is involved. Two additive adapters (e.g. LoRA + LoHa) commute, so they merge correctly in either order. This is probably why the existing tests did not catch the bug: `test_deeply_nested` only stacks additive adapters (LoRA, LoHa, AdaLoRA, LoKr).

**Impact on a real model**

Qwen3-4B (fp32), LoRA (r=16) and OFT (block size 32) on `q/k/v/o_proj`, each trained briefly on WikiText-2, then loaded together into one mixed model. Evaluated on 64 × 256 WikiText-2 test tokens:

| | after 5 merge/unmerge cycles | 13.76 | 92.9% |
| | `merge_and_unload()` | 12.47 | 100% |
| `lora(oft(base))` | unmerged | 12.67 | 100% |
| | `merge_adapter()` | 12.47 | 98.6% |
| | `merge_and_unload()` | 12.67 | 100% |

3830.title: OFT module_dropout has had no effect since #2575: the MultiplicativeDropoutLayer is created but never called
3830.body:
### System Info

peft 0.21.1.dev0 (main @ b8674c8) and peft 0.21.0, torch 2.14.0+cpu, transformers 5.17.0, Python 3.13, Linux

### Information

- [ ] The official example scripts
- [x] My own modified scripts

### Tasks

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder
- [x] My own task or dataset (give details below)

### Reproduction

`OFTConfig.module_dropout` is documented as "the multiplicative dropout probability, by setting OFT blocks to identity during training", and `update_layer` in `oft/layer.py` still builds a `MultiplicativeDropoutLayer(p=module_dropout)` per adapter and stores it in `self.oft_dropout`. Nothing reads it any more: `self.oft_dropout[...]` is not referenced anywhere in the file, so the forward pass is the same with `module_dropout=0.0` and `module_dropout=0.5`.

```python
import torch
from torch import nn

import peft
from peft import OFTConfig, get_peft_model


class M(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.lin = nn.Linear(16, 12)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.lin(x)


torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn(3, 16)
config = OFTConfig(r=4, oft_block_size=0, target_modules=["lin"], init_weights=False, module_dropout=0.5)
model = get_peft_model(M(), config)
model.train()
with torch.no_grad():
    outputs = [model(x) for _ in range(10)]
diffs = [(outputs[0] - o).abs().max().item() for o in outputs[1:]]
print(f"peft {peft.__version__}: max difference between train-mode forward passes: {max(diffs):.4f}")
```

```
peft 0.21.1.dev0: max difference between train-mode forward passes: 0.0000
peft 0.21.0: max difference between train-mode forward passes: 0.0000
peft 0.15.0: max difference between train-mode forward passes: 0.2635
```

In 0.15.0 both `Linear.forward` and `Conv2d.forward` did `orth_rotate = self._cayley_batch(oft_r)` followed by `orth_rotate = dropout(orth_rotate)`. #2575 moved the Cayley transform into `OFTRotationModule` and the `dropout(...)` call did not come along, so since 0.16.0 the setting is silently ignored. The `Embedding` layer never created dropout layers, I left it alone.

With `module_dropout > 0` and the model in train mode, a fraction of the rotation blocks is replaced by the identity in every forward pass, as before #2575 and as the config docstring says. In eval mode and when merging, no dropout is applied.

The fix I have passes the dropout module from the OFT layer into the rotation module: `OFTRotationModule.forward(x, dropout=None)` and `OFTRotationModule.get_weight(dropout=None)` apply it to `orth_rotate` right after the Cayley transform when it is given. `Linear.forward` calls `oft_R(x, dropout=self.oft_dropout[active_adapter])`, `Conv2d.forward` calls `get_weight(dropout=self.oft_dropout[active_adapter])`, and `merge` keeps calling `get_weight()` without it, so `test_merge_layers_is_deterministic_in_train_mode` (#3586) keeps holding. `MultiplicativeDropoutLayer` already skips `block_share=True` (a single sh

3982.title: OFT Conv2d: unmerged and merged outputs differ for kernels larger than 1x1
3982.body:
### System Info

peft main (da530b7), torch 2.7.1, transformers 5.19.0, Python 3.12, CPU

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1 @user-36

### Reproduction

For OFT on a `Conv2d` with a kernel larger than 1x1, the unmerged model and the merged model give different outputs:

```python
import copy, torch
from torch import nn
from peft import OFTConfig, get_peft_model

torch.manual_seed(0)
for k in (1, 3):
    base = nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(4, 8, k, padding=k // 2))
    model = get_peft_model(base, OFTConfig(target_modules=["0"], r=0, oft_block_size=4, init_weights=False))
    x = torch.randn(1, 4, 8, 8)
    with torch.no_grad():
        y = model(x)
        y_merged = copy.deepcopy(model).merge_and_unload()(x)
    print(f"kernel {k}x{k}: max |unmerged - merged| = {(y - y_merged).abs().max():.3g}")
```

```
kernel 1x1: max |unmerged - merged| = 2.38e-07
kernel 3x3: max |unmerged - merged| = 6.55
```

The merged model matches `F.conv2d(x, W @ R.T)`, i.e. the same per-patch rotation OFT applies to `Linear`. The unmerged forward (since #2575) rotates the unfolded input patches and then `F.fold`s them back. `fold` sums overlapping patches, so once patches overlap (any kernel > 1 with stride 1) this is no longer a rotation of the conv weight. Training then optimizes a different function from the one `merge_and_unload()` produces.

The existing OFT `Conv2d` tests don't catch it because `ModelConv2D` feeds a 3x3 input to a 3x3 kernel, so there is a single patch and nothing overlaps.

Separately, OFT merge on a grouped `Conv2d` (`groups > 1`) fails with `RuntimeError: shape '[8, 36]' is invalid for input of size 144`. LoRA raises a clear `NotImplementedError` in that case.

### Expected behavior

Unmerged and merged outputs should match, as they do for 1x1 kernels and `Linear`. Since the fix changes forward outputs for existing conv checkpoints, I'd like your view on the direction before opening a PR. I'm happy to send one: for example, have the conv forward rotate the weight, as merge does, following the peft-method-changes guidance for existing checkpoints.

(Found and reduced with an AI coding assistant, Claude Code. The reproducer and the reference comparison above were run on peft main.)

4039.title: LoRA-FA skips active adapter updates when a second adapter is present
4039.body:
### System Info

- PEFT: `0.21.3.dev0`, unmodified `main` at `b7fa5317bcdc097706ae70f73370392c276a1a2b`
- Python: `3.12.14`
- PyTorch: `2.14.1`
- Transformers: `5.19.0`
- Accelerate: `1.15.0`
- Platform: macOS / arm64, CPU only

### Reproduction

Hi, I noticed that LoRA-FA silently skips updating the active adapter when a second, inactive adapter is present. In the example below, `default` is the only active adapter, and all adapters are added before creating the optimizer. No model downloads or GPU are needed.

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from peft.optimizers import create_lorafa_optimizer

torch.set_num_threads(1)
lora_kwargs = dict(r=2, lora_alpha=4, target_modules=["0"], lora_dropout=0.0)

def run(with_inactive_adapter):
    torch.manual_seed(7)
    model = get_peft_model(
        nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(4, 3, bias=False)), LoraConfig(**lora_kwargs)
    )
    if with_inactive_adapter:
        model.add_adapter("spare", LoraConfig(**lora_kwargs))
    model.set_adapter("default")
    optimizer = create_lorafa_optimizer(model, r=2, lora_alpha=4, lr=0.01)
    b = model.base_model.model[0].lora_B["default"].weight
    before = b.detach().clone()
    x = torch.tensor([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0], [-2.0, 0.5, 1.5, 3.0]])
    model(x).square().mean().backward()
    grad_norm = b.grad.norm().item()
    assert grad_norm > 0
    optimizer.step()
    return grad_norm, (b.detach() - before).abs().max().item()

for extra in [False, True]:
    grad, update = run(extra)
    print(f"inactive_adapter={extra}: grad_norm={grad:.6f}, max_B_update={update:.8f}")
```

Actual output:

```text
inactive_adapter=False: grad_norm=2.217832, max_B_update=0.00999993
inactive_adapter=True: grad_norm=2.217832, max_B_update=0.00000000
```

The active adapter receives the same nonzero gradient in both cases, but its `lora_B` weights remain unchanged in the second case. I also reproduced the skipped updates with a locally initialized tiny Llama causal language model on CPU.

This appears to come from the consecutive-parameter pairing in [`LoraFAOptimizer.step()`](https://github.com/huggingface/peft/blob/b7fa5317bcdc097706ae70f73370392c276a1a2b/src/peft/optimizers/lorafa.py#L116). With two adapters, the order is `A.default, A.spare, B.default, B.spare`, rather than an A/B pair for each adapter. The existing missing-gradient guard then skips both incorrectly assembled pairs.

### Expected behavior

Keeping an inactive adapter loaded should not prevent LoRA-FA from updating the active adapter's `lora_B` weights.

Would a focused fix for this be welcome? I'd be happy to work on the fix and regression tests. I'll wait for maintainer confirmation before opening a PR. Thank you for your time!

### AI assistance

OpenAI Codex assisted with the investigation, reproducer, and drafting this report. The reproducer above was executed locally on CPU against the unmodified PEFT revision listed here. No library patch or PR has been prepared.

3756.body:
### System Info

- peft: main (`fd570a5f`), 0.21.0
- transformers: 5.17.0
- torch: 2.14.0
- accelerate: 1.15.0
- Python: 3.11
- Platform: Linux, CPU only

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1

### Reproduction

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model


class MLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.lin = nn.Linear(8, 8)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.lin(x)


torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn(2, 8)
config = LoraConfig(target_modules=["lin"], r=4, init_lora_weights=False)

model = get_peft_model(MLP(), config, adapter_name="A").eval()
model.add_adapter("B", config)
model.base_model.set_adapter(["A", "B"])  # both adapters active

with torch.no_grad():
    out_both = model(x)
    model.merge_adapter(adapter_names=["A"])  # merge only A; B stays active and unmerged
    out_after_partial_merge = model(x)
    model.unmerge_adapter()
    out_after_unmerge = model(x)

print("active adapters:", model.active_adapters)
print("same output after merging A only:", torch.allclose(out_both, out_after_partial_merge))
print("same output after unmerging again:", torch.allclose(out_both, out_after_unmerge))
print("max abs diff:", (out_both - out_after_partial_merge).abs().max().item())

# The partially merged model behaves like adapter A alone:
model.set_adapter("A")
with torch.no_grad():
    out_only_A = model(x)
print("partially merged output == adapter A alone:", torch.allclose(out_only_A, out_after_partial_merge))
```

Output on `main`:

```
active adapters: ['A', 'B']
same output after merging A only: False
same output after unmerging again: True
max abs diff: 0.5326088070869446
partially merged output == adapter A alone: True
```

`B` is still reported as active (`model.active_adapters == ['A', 'B']`, `get_layer_status()` shows `active_adapters=['A', 'B']`, `merged_adapters=['A']`) but contributes nothing to the output. `unmerge_adapter()` restores the combined output, so the adapter weights are intact; it is purely the forward path. No warning is emitted.

### Cause

Every tuner layer's `forward` short-circuits once anything is merged, e.g. in `lora/layer.py`:

```python
elif self.merged:
    result = self.base_layer(x, *args, **kwargs)
else:
    for active_adapter in self.active_adapters:
        ...
```

so the loop over `self.active_adapters` is skipped entirely. `check_adapters_to_merge` only removes already-merged adapters from the request; nothing checks that the active adapters left unmerged will still be applied. The same pattern exists in all tuners (LoRA, IA³, LoHa, LoKr, OFT, ...). The mirror case, merging an *inactive* adapter while a different one is active, drops the active one for the same reason.

### Expected behavior

Either the unmerged active adapters are still applied on top of the merged weights, or `merge_adapter` refuses / warns when the merge would leave an active adapter unapplied, the same policy `_check_forward_args` already uses

3835.title: delete_adapter skips adapter layers whose module name contains the tuner prefix (e.g. lora_foobar)
3835.body:
### System Info

peft main @ b8674c8 (0.21.1.dev0), torch 2.14.0 (CPU), Python 3.12, macOS.

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1 @maintainer-2

### Reproduction

The module-level `delete_adapter` helper in `src/peft/tuners/tuners_utils.py` (used by `BaseTuner.delete_adapter`, i.e. by every tuner, and exposed as `peft.functional.delete_adapter`) skips modules by an unanchored substring test on the module name:

```python
for key, target in model.named_modules():
    if prefix in key:      # prefix == "lora_"
        continue
    if isinstance(target, layer_cls):
        target.delete_adapter(adapter_name)
```

A base-model module whose *name* happens to contain the prefix (e.g. `lora_foobar`) and that is itself a target of the adapter is therefore never visited. The adapter is removed from `peft_config` and from the other layers, but not from that one:

```python
import torch
from torch import nn
from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model
from peft.tuners.tuners_utils import BaseTunerLayer


class MyModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.lin0 = nn.Linear(10, 10)
        self.lora_foobar = nn.Linear(10, 10)  # ordinary module, name contains "lora_"

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.lora_foobar(self.lin0(x))


config = LoraConfig(target_modules=["lin0", "lora_foobar"], init_lora_weights=False)
model = get_peft_model(MyModel(), config)
model.add_adapter("other", LoraConfig(target_modules=["lin0", "lora_foobar"], init_lora_weights=False))
model.set_adapter("other")
model.delete_adapter("other")

print(list(model.peft_config))  # ['default']
for name, module in model.named_modules():
    if isinstance(module, BaseTunerLayer):
        print(name, sorted(module._get_available_adapters()), module.active_adapters)
# base_model.model.lin0 ['default'] ['default']
# base_model.model.lora_foobar ['default', 'other'] ['other']   <-- deleted adapter still present and still active
print([k for k in model.state_dict() if ".other." in k])
# ['base_model.model.lora_foobar.lora_A.other.weight', 'base_model.model.lora_foobar.lora_B.other.weight']
```

So after `delete_adapter("other")` the `lora_foobar` layer keeps the weights of the deleted adapter (they are also still in `state_dict()`), and because `other` was the active adapter, that layer keeps applying it in `forward`, while `lin0` uses `default`. This is the inconsistent state that `BaseTunerLayer.delete_adapter`'s docstring warns about.

The same substring pitfall was already fixed for the state dict in #3490 (see the `lora_foo` remark in the PR description and `test_prefixes_module_named_like_peft_prefix_not_included`) and `_mark_only_adapters_as_trainable` / `_unload_and_optionally_merge` identify tuner layers structurally; `delete_adapter` still uses the name check. 3728.title: LoRA + torchao: merging several adapters in one call raises UnboundLocalError
3728.body:
### System Info

- `peft` main at `0e8d0ae8`
- `torchao` 0.18.0, PyTorch 2.11.0, Transformers 5.9.0
- Python 3.13.15, Linux, CPU

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1

### Reproduction

Merging more than one adapter in a single call raises `UnboundLocalError` on a torchao quantized layer. `merge_adapter` accepts a list of adapter names, so this is reachable from the public API:

```python
import torch
from torchao.quantization import Int8WeightOnlyConfig
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, TorchAoConfig

from peft import LoraConfig, get_peft_model

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
    "peft-internal-testing/opt-125m",
    quantization_config=TorchAoConfig(Int8WeightOnlyConfig()),
    device_map={"": "cpu"},
)
model = get_peft_model(model, LoraConfig(init_lora_weights=False, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"]))
model.add_adapter("other", LoraConfig(init_lora_weights=False, target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"]))

model.base_model.merge_adapter(adapter_names=["default", "other"])
```

Current result:

```text
  File "/.../src/peft/tuners/tuners_utils.py", line 1321, in merge_adapter
    module.merge(adapter_names=adapter_names, safe_merge=safe_merge)
    ~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/.../src/peft/tuners/lora/torchao.py", line 78, in merge
    weight = weight.dequantize()
             ^^^^^^
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'weight' where it is not associated with a value
```

Merging the two adapters one at a time works, so only the batched call is affected.

### Root cause

`TorchaoLoraLinear.merge` reads the weight once, before the loop, and deletes the local at the end of every iteration:

```python
base_layer = self.get_base_layer()
weight = base_layer.weight

for active_adapter in adapter_names:
    weight = weight.dequantize()
    ...
    del base_layer.weight
    base_layer.weight = weight
    quantize_(base_layer, self.get_apply_tensor_subclass())
    del weight            # <- the name is gone for the next iteration
```

`unmerge` in the same file does the same work but re-reads `base_layer` and `weight` inside the loop, which is why it survives several adapters. Moving those two lines into the loop in `merge` matches `unmerge` and fixes it.

### Expected behavior

`merge_adapter(adapter_names=[...])` merges every listed adapter, as it does for the plain and bitsandbytes LoRA layers.

Duplicate search before filing: `UnboundLocalError`, `torchao adapter_names`, `merge multiple adapters torchao`, plus the open PRs touching `lora/torchao.py`. Nothing covers this. It is separate from the safe merge work in #3710, although it is in the same function, so I mentioned it there.

3182.title: RFC: Improve code to resolve LoRA variants
3182.body:
In PEFT, we support different LoRA variants, e.g. DoRA. Which LoRA variant, if any, should be used is currently implemented in `resolve_lora_variant`. For `lora.Linear`, the method looks like this:

https://github.com/huggingface/peft/blob/76c37d4686cf7245a9a6998fd1e2619d62c9322d/src/peft/tuners/lora/layer.py#L795-L815

This is not very readable, at a glance it's not possible to determine the logic. Therefore, I propose to pattern matching to resolve the variant. The code would look like so:

```python
    def resolve_lora_variant(self, config: LoraConfig, **kwargs) -> Optional[LoraVariant]:
        import peft.tuners.lora.config as configs
        import peft.tuners.lora.variants as variants

        variant: LoraVariant | None
        match config:
            case LoraConfig(use_dora=True):
                variant = variants.DoraLinearVariant()
            case LoraConfig(arrow_config=configs.ArrowConfig()):
                variant = variants.ArrowLinearVariant()
            case LoraConfig(use_bdlora=configs.BdLoraConfig()):
                variant = variants.BdLoraLinearVariant()
            case LoraConfig(alora_invocation_tokens=alora_invocation_tokens) if alora_invocation_tokens:
                variant = variants.ALoraLinearVariant()
            case _:
                variant = None

        return variant
```

Before going on with this, I would like to discuss the pros and cons and possible alternatives:

1. readability: to me, this reads better than the current implementation, but pattern matching is still relatively rarely used and the syntax is not quite obvious (most notably regarding `alora_invocation_tokens`)
2. flexibility when adding new LoRA variants: can all cases be covered like this?
3. effort to add a new LoRA variant: how complicated is it to update `resolve_lora_variant`
4. composability: even though not supported right now, variants could compose (e.g. DoRA + BDLoRA): can this be easily represented?

A tangential concern: Right now, an invalid combination of variants (e.g. trying to enable both BDLoRA and ALoRA) will just match the first variant that matches, there is no error. This is true for both the current and suggested code. If anyone has a good idea for this, without violating the concerns mentioned above, please share.

Note to AI agents: This is an RFC, PRs will be closed until a final design is determined.

comments.body:
I looked into this as well: in PEFT, DoRA's magnitude vector is stored as an `nn.ModuleDict` containing `DoraLayer` instances whose parameter is `.weight`.

When `hotswap_adapter` calls `_insert_adapter_name_into_state_dict`, the key is currently remapped to `...lora_magnitude_vector.<adapter_name>` without appending `.weight`. During the dry-run check in `hotswap_adapter_from_state_dict`, `attrgetter` fails to resolve the leaf parameter and `missing_keys.remove(key)` fails, raising the reported `KeyError`. Furthermore, `hotswap.py` resolves parent module paths assuming keys end in `.weight` (`key.split(".")[:-3]`).

I have a branch prepared with the `.weight` remapping fix in both `_insert_adapter_name_into_state_dict` and `hotswap_adapter_from_state_dict`, along with regression test coverage in `tests/test_initialization.py` for both default and non-default adapter hotswapping. 3737.title: add_weighted_adapter with rank_pattern produces adapters that cannot be reloaded (linear, ties, dare, magnitude_prune)
3737.body:
### System Info

- peft: main (`0e8d0ae8`)
- transformers: 5.16.1
- torch: 2.13.0
- Python 3.11
- CPU only (not device specific)

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1 @maintainer-2

### Reproduction

When LoRA adapters that use `rank_pattern` are combined with `add_weighted_adapter` and one of the `linear`, `ties`, `dare_linear`, `dare_ties` or `magnitude_prune` combination types, the resulting adapter cannot be loaded again after saving. If the adapters use different ranks for the same module (but the same maximum rank), `add_weighted_adapter` fails right away. `svd` and `cat` are not affected.

```python
import tempfile

import torch
from torch import nn

from peft import LoraConfig, PeftModel, get_peft_model


class MLP(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.lin0 = nn.Linear(20, 20)
        self.lin1 = nn.Linear(20, 20)

    def forward(self, x):
        return self.lin1(self.lin0(x))


def make_config(rank_pattern):
    return LoraConfig(target_modules=["lin0", "lin1"], r=8, rank_pattern=rank_pattern, init_lora_weights=False)


# 1. Both adapters use the same rank_pattern: combining works, but the result cannot be reloaded
for combination_type in ["linear", "ties", "dare_linear", "dare_ties", "magnitude_prune", "svd", "cat"]:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    model = get_peft_model(MLP(), make_config({"lin1": 4}), adapter_name="a")
    model.add_adapter("b", make_config({"lin1": 4}))
    kwargs = {} if combination_type in ("linear", "svd", "cat") else {"density": 0.5}
    model.add_weighted_adapter(["a", "b"], [0.5, 0.5], "merged", combination_type=combination_type, **kwargs)
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
        model.save_pretrained(tmp_dir, selected_adapters=["merged"])
        try:
            PeftModel.from_pretrained(MLP(), f"{tmp_dir}/merged")
            print(f"{combination_type}: reload OK")
        except RuntimeError as e:
            print(f"{combination_type}: reload FAILED: {str(e).splitlines()[1].strip()}")

# 2. Same maximum rank, but different ranks for the same module: combining fails immediately
torch.manual_seed(0)
model = get_peft_model(MLP(), make_config({"lin1": 4}), adapter_name="a")
model.add_adapter("b", make_config({}))
try:
    model.add_weighted_adapter(["a", "b"], [0.5, 0.5], "merged", combination_type="linear")
except RuntimeError as e:
    print(f"linear with different per-module ranks: FAILED: {e}")
```

3964.title: An old, unused torchao install makes every LoRA/OFT injection fail with ImportError (e.g. on Colab and Kaggle)
3964.body:
### System Info

- peft: main @ eac46ef (also 0.21.2; affects every release since 0.19.0)
- torchao 0.10.0 (Google Colab's preinstalled version; Kaggle's image also ships one older than 0.16)
- torch 2.13.0+cpu, transformers 5.16.1, Python 3.12, Windows 11 (hit the same error on Colab and Kaggle)

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1 @maintainer-2

### Reproduction

```python
# pip install "torchao==0.10.0"
from torch import nn
from peft import LoraConfig, OFTConfig, get_peft_model

get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(16, 16)), LoraConfig(target_modules=["0"]))
# ImportError: Found an incompatible version of torchao. Found version 0.10.0, but only versions above 0.16.0 are supported

get_peft_model(nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(16, 16)), OFTConfig(target_modules=["0"], r=0, oft_block_size=4))
# same ImportError
```

The model doesn't use torchao at all. The error comes from just having torchao < 0.16 installed.

Since #3101 raised `TORCHAO_MINIMUM_VERSION` to 0.16.0, `is_torchao_available()` raises for older versions instead of returning False. Two call sites run it on every targeted layer *before* checking whether the weight is a torchao tensor:

- `dispatch_torchao` in `src/peft/tuners/lora/torchao.py`
- `resolve_quantization_backend` in `src/peft/utils/quantization_utils.py` (used by OFT and other methods)

So any environment with an older torchao can't use LoRA at all, including `load_lora_weights` in diffusers. Colab ships torchao 0.10.0 by default, so out of the box `get_peft_model` fails there. I hit this in my own project and had to monkeypatch `is_torchao_available` at both binding sites. Several downstream projects are working around it by uninstalling or pinning torchao, for example:

- https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Automodel/issues/4130
- https://github.com/MakazhanAlpamys/Soup/issues/389
- https://github.com/adithya-s-k/FineEnvs/issues/63
- https://github.com/R3gm/SD_diffusers_interactive/issues/43 (diffusers `load_lora_weights`)

### Expected behavior

Layers whose weights aren't torchao tensors should be handled normally whatever torchao version is installed. The "incompatible version" error should only appear when a layer actually uses torchao.

### Proposed fix

Check whether the weight is a torchao tensor before validating the torchao version. That check can be done without importing torchao, by looking for a `torchao` module in the weight's class hierarchy:

```python
def is_torchao_tensor(tensor) -> bool:
    return any(cls.__module__.split(".")[0] == "torchao" for cls in type(tensor).__mro__)
```

Then gate both call sites on it, e.g. in `dispatch_torchao`:

```python
if not hasattr(target_base_layer, "weight") or not is_torchao_tensor(target_base_layer.weight):
    return new_module
```

I tried this locally with torchao 0.10.0. LoRA and OFT on plain layers work again, and a real torchao 0.10 int8-quantized layer (`AffineQuantizedTensor`) still gets the existing informative ImportError, so users who actually quantize with an old t

3675.title: Four of the five diffusers-style tuner docstring examples (LoHa, LoKr, OFT, MiSS) fail as written
3675.body:
### System Info

- peft 0.20.1.dev0 (editable install from `src/`, upstream `main` at `a4c223f3`)
- transformers 5.8.1
- accelerate 1.13.0
- diffusers 0.37.1
- torch 2.12.0+cu130
- Python 3.10.20
- Linux-7.0.0-30-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39

Three of the four failures are version-independent: they raise inside `__init__` of the config dataclass, before any model or checkpoint is touched. The MiSS failure needs a pipeline loaded, but reproduces on any SD 1.5-shaped checkpoint.

### Who can help?

@maintainer-1 

### Reproduction

Five PEFT methods carry an `Example:` block in `model.py` that adapts a `StableDiffusionPipeline`: LoHa, LoKr, OFT, MiSS and HRA. All five reach the API reference via `[[autodoc]]` (`loha.md:90`, `lokr.md:64`, `oft.md:98`, `miss.md:102`, `hra.md:40`), so they are what a reader copies off the docs site. Four cannot run, each for a different reason.

| method | result |
|---|---|
| LoHa | `TypeError: LoHaConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'lora_alpha'` |
| LoKr | `TypeError: LoKrConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'lora_alpha'` |
| OFT | `ValueError: You can only specify either r (8) or oft_block_size (32), but not both simultaneously, because r x oft_block_size == in_features.` |
| MiSS | `TypeError: Target module Conv2d(64, 64, kernel_size=(1, 1), stride=(1, 1)) is not supported. Currently, only torch.nn.Linear (optionally quantized) is supported.` |
| HRA | runs |

To reproduce, copy the `Example:` block out of any of the four `model.py` files and run it. LoHa, LoKr and OFT fail at the first config, before the pipeline is fetched:

```py
>>> from peft import LoHaConfig
>>> LoHaConfig(task_type="SEQ_2_SEQ_LM", r=8, lora_alpha=32, target_modules=["k_proj"])
TypeError: LoHaConfig.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'lora_alpha'
```

**LoHa, LoKr — `lora_alpha` is not a field on either config.** `src/peft/tuners/loha/model.py`, `src/peft/tuners/lokr/model.py`, two call sites each. The field is `alpha`; `git log -S lora_alpha` on both config files is empty. Copied from a LoRA block and never adjusted — broken since `7a5f17f3` (#956) and `884b1ac3` (#978). `tests/test_stablediffusion.py` passes `"alpha": 32` here, so this is a rename rather than a deletion.

**OFT — `r=8` collides with the default `oft_block_size=32`.** `OFTConfig` defaults to `r=0`, `oft_block_size=32`, and `oft/config.py` enforces an exclusive-or:

```py
if not (self.r != 0) ^ (self.oft_block_size != 0):
    raise ValueError(...)
```

**MiSS — targets modules MiSS cannot adapt.** `src/peft/tuners/miss/model.py` targets `proj_in` and `proj_out`, which are `Conv2d` in SD 1.5. MiSS supports `Linear` only, unlike HRA's `HRAConv2d`. The block is a verbatim copy of HRA's — only the clas
